name: Voyager
institution: NVIDIA / Caltech / UT Austin / Stanford / ASU (MineDojo team; authors: Guanzhi Wang, Yuqi Xie, Yunfan Jiang, Ajay Mandlekar, Chaowei Xiao, Yuke Zhu, Linxi "Jim" Fan, Anima Anandkumar)
type: academic (peer-reviewed paper, arXiv preprint; MIT-licensed open-source code)
what_evolved: Tools技能 (skill library) + Context记忆与提示. An ever-growing library of executable-code skills is the evolving carrier; model weights are NOT evolved (GPT-4 used as black-box, no fine-tuning). Composition of simpler skills compounds abilities over time.
skill_as_artifact: Yes. Each skill is an independent reusable artifact: a self-contained executable code program plus a natural-language description, verified and committed to a persistent skill library (stored as folders) for later retrieval/composition in similar situations.
skill_encoding: Executable code (JavaScript programs targeting the Mineflayer bot API, wrapped with Voyager utility functions), each paired with an NL description. Code is chosen as action space to express temporally-extended, compositional behaviors. Indexed by embedding of its description.
skill_granularity: 子任务workflow (sub-task programs). Each skill accomplishes a temporally-extended sub-task (e.g. 'craft wooden pickaxe', 'hunt zombie'); complex skills are synthesized by composing simpler programs.
how_method: reward-based (environment/exec feedback as text reward) + rollout_optimization (text/code-space optimization via iterative prompting, non-gradient). Iterative prompting mechanism incorporates environment feedback, execution errors, and self-verification to improve programs; no gradient-based training or parameter access.
learning_signal_source: 环境反馈 (environment execution feedback + execution errors) + 自我反思 (GPT-4 self-verification as critic) + 成败轨迹 (execution success/failure). Learning is entirely in-context via black-box GPT-4 queries.
reward_granularity: hybrid (process-level execution-error feedback during code iteration + outcome-level self-verification of task achievement)
learning_paradigm: online; in-context lifelong learning via black-box LLM (no parameter training, so on/off-policy N/A). Continual skill accumulation during a single lifelong run with checkpointing/resume.
when_evolve: intra-test-time (online, during task execution). Voyager performs continuous lifelong learning, progressively acquiring/storing skills while playing in one open-ended session.
trigger: curriculum-driven (GPT-4 automatic curriculum proposes next exploration tasks based on agent state + progress, an in-context novelty search) + failure-triggered iterative prompting (regenerates code on execution error or failed self-verification).
library_structure: 向量库 + 技能文件. Each skill = a folder containing executable code + description; skills indexed by vector embedding of their description for similarity search.
retrieval_method: 语义相似度 (semantic similarity: embed skill description, retrieve top-5 relevant skills for a new task) + 代码直接复用 (direct code reuse / composition of simpler programs). The skill library also serves as a plug-and-play asset that boosts other methods (e.g. AutoGPT).
validation: execution-based (run code in Minecraft; observe environment feedback + execution errors) + LLM-judge / validation gating (GPT-4 self-verification acts as critic to confirm task achievement; only verified skills are committed to the library).
error_correction: self-revision (iterative prompting regenerates/edits the program using the error message or critique as feedback; bounded multi-round correction before a skill is accepted or rejected).
test_env: Minecraft (via Mineflayer Node.js bot + Mineflayer-collectblock; connects to a Fabric-modded Minecraft 1.19 instance).
backbone_model: GPT-4 (black-box API queries for curriculum, code generation, and self-verification); ablation shows GPT-4 far outperforms GPT-3.5 for code generation.
metrics: skill_library_growth (new unique items discovered; library size), generalization (zero-shot transfer to unseen tasks in a new world), sample_efficiency (prompting iterations to reach milestones), success_rate (tech-tree tool tiers, task completion), exploration (unique items, map distance traveled, tech-tree milestones unlocked).
key_results: Obtains 3.3x more unique items (63 within 160 iterations), travels 2.3x longer distances, and unlocks key tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior SOTA (wooden 15.3x, stone 8.5x, iron 6.4x faster; Voyager is the ONLY method to unlock the diamond tier). Zero-shot: solves ALL unseen tasks in a new world while baselines solve NONE within 50 iterations. Skill library also plug-and-play boosts AutoGPT. Ablation: each module matters and GPT-4 >> GPT-3.5.
limitations: transferability (skills are JavaScript/Mineflayer-bound to Minecraft, hard to port to other games/real robots), scalability (depends on costly/slow GPT-4 API calls), controllability (open-ended novelty-search curriculum may produce non-useful skills; no external goal alignment), eval-hacking risk (self-verification by same LLM that generates code). No model-parameter learning, so all knowledge is in-context/contextual; catastrophic forgetting is alleviated but not transfer across domains.
